title: Monoidal and adjunction normalization of derived ringed-topos comparisons
statement:
Let $X\xrightarrow fY\xrightarrow gZ$ be morphisms of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism], presented by sites small in the universe of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaves of commutative rings $A_X,A_Y,A_Z$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the K-flat derived tensor and pullbacks of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], and the K-injective direct images and normalized comparisons $\kappa_{g,f}:R(gf)_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Rg_*Rf_*$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Write $P_h=Lh^*$, $R_h=Rh_*$, and give $P_h\dashv R_h$ the canonical derived adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Write $t_h:P_h(U\otimes^L V)\xrightarrow{\sim}P_hU\otimes^LP_hV$ for the canonical tensor comparison, and $e_h:P_hA_{\mathrm{target}}\xrightarrow{\sim}A_{\mathrm{source}}$ for its unit comparison.

These comparisons make $P_h$ a symmetric strong monoidal functor: $t_h,e_h$ commute with the derived tensor associators, both unitors, and the symmetry. The associator is induced by $(x\otimes y)\otimes z\mapsto x\otimes(y\otimes z)$ and the symmetry by $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{pq}y\otimes x$ in degrees $p,q$.

There is a canonical comparison $c_{f,g}:P_{gf}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_fP_g$, computed by ordinary module pullback composition on K-flat complexes with flat terms. It is monoidal: for $U,V\in D(A_Z)$,
$$t_{f;P_gU,P_gV}\circ P_f(t_{g;U,V})\circ c_{f,g,U\otimes^LV}=(c_{f,g,U}\otimes^Lc_{f,g,V})\circ t_{gf;U,V},$$
and $e_f\circ P_f(e_g)\circ c_{f,g,A_Z}=e_{gf}$. The comparison $\kappa_{g,f}$ is adjunction-compatible: under $c_{f,g}$ and $\kappa_{g,f}$ the canonical adjunction for $gf$ is the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. In particular its counit is
$$\varepsilon_{gf,E}=\varepsilon_{f,E}\circ P_f(\varepsilon_{g,R_fE})$$
under those comparisons. The canonical comparisons $P_{\mathrm{id}}\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $R_{\mathrm{id}}\cong\mathrm{id}$ identify the tensor comparisons and the adjunction with those of the identity functor and identity adjunction. Finally, if two ringed-topos morphisms with the same source and target are related by a 2-isomorphism of their underlying geometric morphisms whose structural ring maps commute with that 2-isomorphism, then this specified isomorphism induces a monoidal isomorphism of their derived pullbacks and the corresponding adjunction-compatible isomorphism of their derived direct images. All these assertions hold without flatness of the structural ring maps or boundedness of the complexes.

proof.text: For a ring sheaf $A$, write $Q_A:K(A)\to D(A)$ and let $\mathcal P_A$ be the flat-term K-flat complexes. The cited descent theorem identifies $D(A)$ with the localization of $\mathcal P_A$ at quasi-isomorphisms. The cited total-tensor model says that $P\otimes Q$ lies in $\mathcal P_A$ for $P,Q\in\mathcal P_A$ and represents their derived tensor. The cited derived-pullback comparison identifies $P_hQ_AP$ with $Q(h^*P)$ naturally on this class, and the tensor-pullback theorem says $h^*P$ again lies in the corresponding resolving class. Thus repeated tensor products and successive pullbacks may all be computed on the same representatives; no intermediate replacement is needed. Equalities between natural transformations of derived functors can be checked on these representatives: every derived object is isomorphic to one of them, and naturality conjugates its component equality by that isomorphism. For transformations defined on representatives, use the cited localization universal property to descend them.

Use the symmetric monoidal structure on $D(A)$ of the cited ringed-site theorem: its unit is $A[0]$, its associator is ordinary reassociation of total tensors, and its symmetry on bidegree $(p,q)$ has sign $(-1)^{pq}$. On $P,Q\in\mathcal P_A$, the canonical $t_h$ is the localization of the cochain map $c_{h;P,Q}$ of the cited cochain-coherence node; $e_h$ is the localized action map $h^*A[0]\cong A'[0]$. That node states the cochain associator, both unitor, and signed-symmetry squares. Localizing those squares gives precisely the corresponding squares for $t_h,e_h$ on representatives. Step 1 then gives them on arbitrary derived objects (for the associator take three representatives). Their invertibility and naturality are supplied by the tensor-pullback theorem. Hence these particular comparisons, with the inverse-structure-map convention in the strong monoidal definition, make $P_h$ symmetric strong monoidal.

source.place: Tags 0FPT (lemma-symmetric-monoidal-derived), 07A4; representative coherence of the displayed total-complex comparison

proof.text:
For $P\in\mathcal P_{A_Z}$, both $P_{gf}QP$ and $P_fP_gQP$ are computed respectively by $(gf)^*P$ and $f^*g^*P$: $g^*P$ is still flat-term K-flat. Localize the ordinary comparison $a_P:(gf)^*P\cong f^*g^*P$ specified in the cochain-coherence node. It is natural on the homotopy category and descends uniquely by the localization universal property to $c_{f,g}$, using the resolving-class equivalence of step 1. For $P,Q\in\mathcal P_{A_Z}$, that cochain node gives
$$(a_P\otimes a_Q)c_{gf;P,Q}=c_{f;g^*P,g^*Q}\,f^*(c_{g;P,Q})\,a_{\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)}.$$
All complexes in this equation are valid representatives by step 1. Localization gives the asserted tensor equation for $c_{f,g}$ on $QP,QQ$; naturality and essential surjectivity give it for every $U,V$.

The comparison $a$ in step 3 is inverse to multiplication of the two scalar-extension factors. On the unit it sends $t\otimes z$ to $t\otimes(1\otimes z)$, with inverse $t\otimes(s\otimes z)\mapsto t f^\sharp(s)\otimes z$ (inverse-image identifications understood). Applying $f^*(e_g)$ and then $e_f$ therefore gives $t(gf)^\sharp(z)$, which is also $e_{gf}(t\otimes z)$. Pure tensors determine sheaf-linear maps by the cited section calculus. This proves $e_fP_f(e_g)c_{f,g,A_Z}=e_{gf}$ after localization. The unit complexes and their pullbacks are valid flat-term K-flat representatives by the model and pullback facts in step 1.

source.place: Tag 03D8 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules), scalar multiplication on the unit; Tag 03EL (lemma-tensor-product-pullback)

proof.text:
Let $\epsilon_h^0:h^*h_*\to1$ denote the ordinary module counit. Under $a_P:(gf)^*P\cong f^*g^*P$ and $(gf)_*=g_*f_*$, the ordinary transpose of $b:P\to g_*f_*I$ is
$$\epsilon_{f,I}^0\,f^*(\epsilon_{g,f_*I}^0\,g^*b)\,a_P.$$
Indeed the module adjunction is inverse-image transposition followed by scalar extension. The cited geometric-module transport fixes that inverse-image transposition on underlying sheaves, and the section calculus fixes scalar-extension insertion as $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. The two successive transpositions therefore insert $1\otimes(1\otimes x)$; $a$ identifies this with $1\otimes x$. Multiplication of a general outer scalar gives the same result on every $t\otimes x$, which determines the map. The geometric part is precisely composition of the given inverse-image Hom bijections. Thus these Hom bijections agree, degree by degree. The termwise-adjunction theorem passes this equality to homotopy classes. This verifies the ordinary adjunction normalization of the specific scalar-association comparison, rather than choosing a different comparison from abstract adjoint uniqueness.

Write $\alpha_{h,P}:P_hQP\cong Qh^*P$ for the flat-term K-flat comparison and $\beta_{h,I}:Qh_*I\cong R_hQI$ for the K-injective right-derived unit. The inverse of the canonical derived Hom bijection, denoted $\Theta_h$, satisfies
$$\Theta_h(\beta_{h,I}\,Qb)=Q(\epsilon_{h,I}^0\,h^*b)\,\alpha_{h,P}\quad(b:P\to h_*I).$$
This is the explicit formula of the cited pre-derived-adjunction theorem with target resolution $I\xrightarrow{1}I$ and source resolution $P\xrightarrow{1}P$, not an extra compatibility assumption. The derived pullback theorem makes $\alpha_{h,P}$ invertible and the right-derived-functor definition makes $\beta_{h,I}$ invertible. The canonical derived adjunction in the item is the everywhere-defined adjunction assembled from these same Hom bijections. For a quasi-isomorphism $s:P'\to P$ with $P'$ flat-term K-flat, naturality gives
$$\Theta_h(\beta_{h,I}Qb\,(Qs)^{-1})=Q(\epsilon_{h,I}^0h^*b)\,\alpha_{h,P'}\,(P_hQs)^{-1}.$$
Thus the formula also treats fraction representatives.

Fix a K-injective $I$ on $X$, and choose a K-injective resolution $j:f_*I\to J$ on $Y$. The pushforward-composition node states that $g_*j$ is a quasi-isomorphism and that $\kappa_{g,f,QI}$ is its localized class under the resolution identifications. No assertion that $f_*I$ is K-injective is needed. To compare the derived Hom bijections on every morphism into $R_{gf}QI\cong Qg_*f_*I$, represent a morphism out of $QN$ by a right fraction $N\xleftarrow{s}P\xrightarrow{b}g_*f_*I$. Resolve $P$ once more by a flat-term K-flat complex and compose the denominator and numerator with that resolution. This is again the same fraction. Existence follows from the cited calculus-of-fractions and K-flat-resolution nodes. It therefore suffices, by the naturality in step 6, to do the calculation for an actual map $b:P\to g_*f_*I$ with $P$ flat-term K-flat.

source.place: Tag 0D6E, normalized comparison on K-injectives; derived.tex fraction calculus, as used in Tag 0FND

proof.text:
Put $v=\epsilon_{g,f_*I}^0g^*b:g^*P\to f_*I$. After applying $\kappa$, the map represented by $b$ is represented on $Y$'s chosen K-injective resolution by $(g_*j)b:P\to g_*J$. Step 6 for $g$ sends it to
$$Q(\epsilon_{g,J}^0\,g^*((g_*j)b))\,\alpha_{g,P}=Q(jv)\,\alpha_{g,P}.$$
The equality is exactly naturality of the ordinary counit at $j$: $\epsilon_{g,J}^0g^*(g_*j)=j\epsilon_{g,f_*I}^0$. Under the isomorphism $QJ\cong R_fQI$, the map $Q(jv)$ is $\beta_{f,I}Qv$. Apply step 6 for $f$ to it. This is permitted because $g^*P$ is flat-term K-flat by the tensor-pullback node. The resulting composite transpose is
$$Q(\epsilon_{f,I}^0 f^*v)\,\alpha_{f,g^*P}\,P_f(\alpha_{g,P}).$$
Explicitly the identification is $\iota_J=\beta_{f,I}(Qj)^{-1}:QJ\cong R_fQI$, so $\iota_JQ(jv)=\beta_{f,I}Qv$; only invertibility of the quasi-isomorphism $Qj$ is used.

source.place: Tags 0D6E and 07A6; counit naturality in the representative calculation of Tag 0FPI (lemma-adjoints-push-pull-compatibility)

proof.text:
Precompose the last map of step 8 with $c_{f,g,QP}$. By the construction in step 3, the composite of $c_{f,g,QP}$ with the two $\alpha$-comparisons is $Q(a_P)\alpha_{gf,P}$. Hence the result is
$$Q(\epsilon_{f,I}^0 f^*(\epsilon_{g,f_*I}^0g^*b)a_P)\,\alpha_{gf,P}.$$
By the ordinary calculation of step 5 this is $Q(\epsilon_{gf,I}^0(gf)^*b)\alpha_{gf,P}$, which step 6 identifies with $\Theta_{gf}(\beta_{gf,I}Qb)$. Step 7 and naturality give the equality for every derived morphism out of every object into $R_{gf}QI$. Every $E\in D(A_X)$ has a K-injective representative, so the same equality holds for every $E$. This proves that under precisely $c$ and the specified $\kappa$, the canonical Hom bijection for $gf$ equals the composite canonical Hom bijection. Since units and counits are the transposes of identities, this is compatibility of the actual adjunctions.

source.place: Tags 0D6D, 0D6E, 07A6, 0FPI; derived.tex Tag 0FND, representative Hom formula

proof.text:
Apply the definition of composite adjunction to the equality of Hom bijections just proved. In full, the counit formula is
$$\varepsilon_{gf,E}=\varepsilon_{f,E}\,P_f(\varepsilon_{g,R_fE})\,c_{f,g,R_gR_fE}\,P_{gf}(\kappa_{g,f,E}).$$
Its domain is $P_{gf}R_{gf}E$ and codomain is $E$. With these comparisons suppressed, it is exactly the counit formula stated in the item. The unit is likewise the composite unit because the same bijection sends the identity of the left-adjoint value to its unit.

For the identity geometric morphism with identity structural ring map, ordinary module pullback is $A\otimes_A-$ and its action isomorphism to the identity has inverse $x\mapsto1\otimes x$. The sheaf tensor section calculus shows that under this isomorphism $c_{\mathrm{id};P,Q}$ sends $x\otimes y$ to itself and the unit map sends $1$ to $1$. These equalities localize on flat-term K-flat representatives, so identify the derived tensor comparisons with those of the identity. Ordinary direct image is the identity. Its right-derived comparison on $I$ is $QI\cong QI$ using the identity K-injective resolution; step 6 reduces to the identity Hom bijection. Thus the canonical identity comparisons identify both unit and counit with identity maps, as required by the definition of identity adjunction.

source.place: Tag 03D7, identity ringed-topos morphism; sites-cohomology.tex Tags 07A4, 07A6

proof.text:
Let $h,k:X\to Y$ and let the specified geometric 2-isomorphism have inverse-image component $\theta:h^{-1}\cong k^{-1}$. Naturality at addition, multiplication, zero, one, and scalar action, together with the canonical finite-product comparisons, identifies the transported ring and module structures in the geometric-module-transport node. Commutation with the structural ring maps makes
$$d_M:h^*M\longrightarrow k^*M,\qquad s\otimes x\longmapsto s\otimes\theta_M(x)$$
well-defined; the inverse uses $\theta^{-1}$. This is an equation on generalized sheaf elements using the transported-ring identifications. The section calculus proves naturality and equality of maps from their pure-tensor values. Tensor compatibility is the two-line equality sending $s\otimes(x\otimes y)$ along either route to $(s\otimes\theta x)\otimes(1\otimes\theta y)$; unit compatibility follows from $s\otimes a\mapsto s h^\sharp(a)=s k^\sharp(\theta a)$. The right component is the geometric mate of $\theta$; the geometric-module Hom formula and the scalar-extension insertion show that it induces the corresponding module direct-image isomorphism and intertwines the ordinary Hom bijections. These computations work termwise, including the signed tensor differential.

source.place: Tags 03D7 and 03EL, intrinsic inverse-image and scalar-extension constructions; categories.tex adjoint conjugation

proof.text: Apply $d$ termwise to flat-term K-flat representatives. The derived-pullback identifications and the localization universal property give a natural isomorphism $P_h\cong P_k$, with inverse induced by $d^{-1}$. Localize the tensor and unit equalities in step 12 and use step 1 to get a monoidal isomorphism on every derived object. On direct images use the same K-injective representative $I$ of the source object for both functors, and apply the right component of the given geometric 2-isomorphism to $I$; this gives a chain isomorphism $h_*I\cong k_*I$ and hence the canonical derived direct-image isomorphism. In the formula of step 6 the ordinary transposes agree by step 12, so their localized transposes agree. Fractions and K-injective representatives as in step 7 cover all arguments, proving adjunction compatibility. The conjugate bijection identifies this isomorphism with the corresponding adjunction mate, fixing its normalization. All representatives here are unbounded ones; the only pullback preservation used is the flat-term K-flat theorem, which imposes no flatness on structural ring maps.
